description: List the top films by share of inventory copies, keeping every film whose copy count reaches the 10th-highest count, so ties at the cut are all included.

a.request: For each film in the inventory, show its `film_id`, its number of copies (inventory records), and its share of all inventory copies (its copy count divided by the total number of copies across all films, unrounded). Sort from highest share to lowest and return the top 10 films, plus every other film whose copy count equals that of the 10th film, so no film tied at the cutoff is left out.
a.sql:
WITH film_copy_counts AS (
  SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS copy_count
  FROM inventory
  GROUP BY film_id
), ranked AS (
  SELECT film_id, copy_count,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY copy_count DESC, film_id) AS row_num,
         NTH_VALUE(copy_count, 10) OVER (
           ORDER BY copy_count DESC, film_id
           ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
         ) AS tenth_copy_count
  FROM film_copy_counts
), total AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_copies
  FROM inventory
)
SELECT r.film_id,
       r.copy_count,
       r.copy_count / t.total_copies AS copy_share
FROM ranked r
CROSS JOIN total t
WHERE r.row_num <= 10 OR r.copy_count = r.tenth_copy_count
ORDER BY r.copy_count DESC, r.film_id;

b.request: List each film’s ID, inventory copy count, and unrounded share of all inventory copies, ordered by share descending; include every film tied at the 10th-highest copy count
b.sql:
WITH film_copies AS (
  SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count
  FROM film f
  LEFT JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id
), ranked AS (
  SELECT film_id, copy_count,
         copy_count / SUM(copy_count) OVER () AS share_of_inventory,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY copy_count DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM film_copies
)
SELECT film_id, copy_count, share_of_inventory
FROM ranked
WHERE copy_rank <= 10
ORDER BY share_of_inventory DESC;

c.request: What are the top 10 films by number of copies in our inventory? For each, show the `film_id`, how many copies we have, and what share of all inventory copies that is (copies divided by the total number of copies, unrounded), with the highest share first. List the top films by share of inventory copies, keeping every film whose copy count reaches the 10th-highest count, so ties at the cut are all included.
c.sql: SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS copy_count, COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) AS share_of_inventory FROM inventory GROUP BY film_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= (SELECT copy_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS copy_count FROM inventory GROUP BY film_id ORDER BY copy_count DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) AS tenth) ORDER BY share_of_inventory DESC

d.request: Which films have the highest share of inventory copies, including every film tied at the 10th-highest copy count? Show each film’s `film_id`, copy count, and share of all inventory copies (copy count divided by the total, unrounded), with the highest share first.
d.sql:
WITH film_copy_counts AS (
  SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count
  FROM film AS f
  JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id
), ranked AS (
  SELECT film_id, copy_count,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY copy_count DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM film_copy_counts
)
SELECT film_id,
       copy_count,
       copy_count / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory) AS inventory_share
FROM ranked
WHERE copy_rank <= 10
ORDER BY inventory_share DESC;
